dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: An inductively generated admissible-run relation on a format, inputs x and y, and a trace. Its supplied constructor requires a nearest-representable rounding of x+y, adjacent-representable roundings of the two residuals, and no-overflow conditions for all three exact quantities.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target assumes an admissible run for fmt, x, y, and tr, thereby constraining the trace fields through the three rounding steps and overflow premises.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: A trace type constructed from three real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The quantified trace tr supplies three real fields, denoted s, t, and e.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: The third real field of a trace.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is tr.e, the rounded second residual and final correction term.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: The first real field of a trace.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is tr.s, the rounded value of the exact sum x+y.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: The second real field of a trace.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: This is tr.t, the rounded value of the exact residual s-x.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: A finite radix-format record consisting of a natural radix beta, natural precision, integer exponent bounds emin and emax, and proofs that 2 <= beta, 0 < precision, and emin <= emax.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The theorem is universally quantified over every format satisfying these embedded parameter restrictions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: The radix beta of a format cast from a natural number to a real number.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the real base used in division, mantissa bounds, and powers.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real mantissa bound beta^precision, where beta is cast to a real and precision is a natural exponent.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It bounds integer mantissas strictly and appears in the size condition and overflow threshold.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: The scale at integer exponent q, defined as beta^q using integer exponentiation over the reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines represented values m beta^q, the witness-dependent bound on |y|, and the overflow threshold.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: A representation witness for a real x in fmt. It contains integers m and q satisfying -beta^precision < m < beta^precision, emin <= q <= emax, and x = m beta^q, with m cast to a real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Such witnesses define representability; the special existential hypothesis also reads the witness exponent q.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: The integer exponent field of a representation witness.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The existential size condition uses this particular exponent to scale its upper bound on |y|.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: Representability of x in fmt, defined as nonemptiness of the type of representation witnesses for x.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The target assumes x and y are representable, and the run relation requires s, t, and e to be representable.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: The constructor for an admissible run. It requires s to minimize absolute error among all representable values for x+y; t to have no representable value strictly between it and s-x; e to have no representable value strictly between it and y-t; and no overflow for x+y, s-x, and y-t.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the precise mathematical content of the run hypothesis used by the proposition.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: The constructor mapping three real numbers to a trace whose fields are those numbers in order.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It identifies a trace as the ordered triple (s,t,e).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: The first field of a format, namely its natural radix beta.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the real radix and all radix powers.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: The format constructor taking beta and precision in the natural numbers, emin and emax in the integers, and proofs of 2 <= beta, 0 < precision, and emin <= emax.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures every quantified format carries exactly these basic radix, precision, and exponent-range restrictions.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: The second field of a format, namely its natural precision.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the natural exponent in the mantissa bound beta^precision.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018
dependency_coverage.meaning: The constructor of a representation witness from integer mantissa m and exponent q, strict mantissa bounds, inclusive exponent bounds, and the equality x = m beta^q.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expands every representability assumption and the existential representation of x into explicit integer data and inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef019
dependency_coverage.meaning: The fourth field of a format, namely the maximum integer exponent emax.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the upper exponent limit for representations and is used in the no-overflow threshold.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020
dependency_coverage.meaning: The third field of a format, namely the minimum integer exponent emin.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the lower exponent limit for representation witnesses.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021
dependency_coverage.meaning: No overflow for a real z means |z| < beta^precision beta^emax.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The run hypothesis imposes this strict bound on x+y, s-x, and y-t.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef022
dependency_coverage.meaning: An adjacent-representable rounding relation: rounded is representable, and no representable candidate c satisfies rounded < c <= exact or exact <= c < rounded.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It constrains t relative to s-x and e relative to y-t, but does not require global nearest rounding or prescribe which side of the exact value is chosen.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef023
dependency_coverage.meaning: Nearest-representable rounding in fmt, obtained by applying the generic absolute-error minimization relation to fmt-representability.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires s to be a globally nearest representable value to x+y, with ties permitted.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef024
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a predicate R, exact value a, and rounded value r, this means R(r) and |a-r| <= |a-c| for every c satisfying R(c).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With R equal to format representability, it gives the exact global absolute-error property of s.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It combines the four asserted conclusions and combines component conditions inside rounding and representation-related definitions.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: The division operation extracted from a division-and-inverse monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It provides ordinary real division in beta/2.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Propositional equality.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It states the three exact identities t=s-x, e=y-t, and s+e=x+y, as well as represented-value equalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Exists
dependency_coverage.meaning: Existential quantification over a type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It asserts the existence of a particular representation witness for x satisfying the bound involving that witness's exponent.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The addition operation selected by a heterogeneous-addition instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real arguments it denotes ordinary addition in x+y and s+e.

dependency_coverage.name: HDiv.hDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: The division operation selected by a heterogeneous-division instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real arguments it denotes ordinary real division, specifically beta/2.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The multiplication operation selected by a heterogeneous-multiplication instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real arguments it denotes ordinary multiplication in represented values, bounds, and overflow thresholds.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: The subtraction operation selected by a heterogeneous-subtraction instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For real arguments it denotes ordinary subtraction in residuals, errors, and beta^precision-beta/2.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: The non-strict order relation supplied by an LE instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For reals and integers it supplies the inequalities in the size condition, error bound, nearest-rounding condition, and exponent bounds.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The radix and precision are natural numbers, and natural numerals and natural powers are used in the format definitions.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instAtLeastTwoHAddOfNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: A proof-producing instance showing that n+1 is at least two when n is nonzero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It participates only in elaborating the numeral 2 for the real expression beta/2; it adds no independent mathematical hypothesis.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.instNeZeroSucc
dependency_coverage.meaning: A proof that every natural successor n+1 is nonzero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports elaboration of the numeral 2 and contributes no additional proposition-level restriction.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Interpretation of a natural numeral in a type carrying the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets 2 as a real number in beta/2 and interprets auxiliary natural numerals used by typeclass elaboration.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The inputs, trace fields, represented values, scales, bounds, and errors are all scalar real quantities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The ordinary addition operation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the mathematical sums x+y and s+e.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: The additive-group structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies negation and subtraction structure needed by the real absolute-value operation.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instDivInvMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real multiplication, inverse, division, and integer-power structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies real division in beta/2 and integer powers beta^q, including reciprocal powers when q is negative.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual non-strict order on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All real-valued <= comparisons use the standard real order.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The ordinary multiplication operation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It multiplies mantissas by scales and forms the size and overflow bounds.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNatCast
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical embedding of natural numbers into the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It converts the natural radix beta and the numeral 2 into real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary real subtraction, defined as addition of the additive inverse.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms s-x, y-t, s-(x+y), exact-minus-rounded errors, and beta^precision-beta/2.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: The lattice structure induced by the usual order on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the definition of absolute value as the maximum of a real and its negation.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: Absolute value, defined as max(a,-a) in a lattice-ordered additive group.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For reals it yields |y|, rounding errors, the final error |s-(x+y)|, and no-overflow magnitudes.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The adapter turning an ordinary homogeneous addition operation into heterogeneous-addition notation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures all displayed additions of reals are ordinary real addition.

dependency_coverage.name: instHDiv
dependency_coverage.meaning: The adapter turning ordinary homogeneous division into heterogeneous-division notation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures beta/2 is ordinary real division.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The adapter turning ordinary homogeneous multiplication into heterogeneous-multiplication notation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures the products in representations and bounds are ordinary real products.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: The adapter turning ordinary homogeneous subtraction into heterogeneous-subtraction notation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It ensures all residual and error differences are ordinary real subtraction.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatAtLeastTwo
dependency_coverage.meaning: An OfNat instance that interprets a natural numeral n in a type with a natural-number cast when n is known to be at least two.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It converts the literal 2 to the real number 2 in beta/2 and introduces no new mathematical condition.

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical interpretation of each natural numeral as itself in Nat.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the auxiliary natural literals used while elaborating the real numeral 2.

dependency_coverage.name: DivInvMonoid.toZPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: The integer-power operation associated with a division-and-inverse monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets beta^q for integer representation exponents and beta^emax in the overflow threshold.

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: The exponentiation operation selected by a heterogeneous-power instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses both the natural power beta^precision and integer powers beta^q.

dependency_coverage.name: Int
dependency_coverage.meaning: The type of integers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Mantissas, representation exponents, and format exponent bounds are integers.

dependency_coverage.name: Monoid.toNatPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: The natural-power operation associated with a monoid.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets beta^precision with natural precision in the mantissa bound.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat.cast
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical cast from natural numbers into a type with a NatCast structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It realizes the real radix beta and real numeral 2.

dependency_coverage.name: Nonempty
dependency_coverage.meaning: The proposition that a type has at least one inhabitant.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Representability asserts that at least one representation witness exists without selecting it; the separate existential condition does select a witness whose exponent is used.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: The multiplicative monoid structure on the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies natural powers of the real radix and underlies the integer-power structure.

dependency_coverage.name: instHPow
dependency_coverage.meaning: The adapter turning a homogeneous power operation into heterogeneous-power notation.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It connects real natural and integer powers to the notation used in mantissaBound and scale.

dependency_coverage.name: Int.cast
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical cast from integers into a type with an IntCast structure.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It views integer mantissas as real numbers in their bounds and represented-value equations.

dependency_coverage.name: Int.instLEInt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual non-strict order on integers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives emin <= q <= emax and the format condition emin <= emax.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict order relation supplied by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses strict mantissa bounds, strict no-overflow bounds, and strict portions of the adjacency relation.

dependency_coverage.name: Neg.neg
dependency_coverage.meaning: The negation operation supplied by a Neg instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It forms the lower mantissa bound -beta^precision and participates in real absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instIntCast
dependency_coverage.meaning: The canonical embedding of integers into the real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets integer mantissas as reals.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLT
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual strict order on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It governs strict mantissa inequalities, no-overflow inequalities, and strict interval endpoints in adjacent rounding.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instNeg
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary additive negation on real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies -beta^precision, subtraction, and absolute value.

dependency_coverage.name: instLENat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual non-strict order on natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the format restriction 2 <= beta.

dependency_coverage.name: instLTNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The usual strict order on natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the format restriction 0 < precision.

dependency_coverage.name: Not
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical negation, defined as implication to falsehood.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It asserts that no representable candidate lies in either forbidden interval between an adjacent rounded value and its exact value.

dependency_coverage.name: Or
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical disjunction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It combines the two possible order orientations in the forbidden-between condition for adjacent rounding.

binders: fmt ranges over finite radix formats with natural radix beta, natural precision p, integer exponent bounds emin and emax, and embedded proofs 2 <= beta, 0 < p, and emin <= emax.
x and y range over scalar real numbers.
tr ranges over triples of real numbers; write tr=(s,t,e), where s, t, and e are respectively its first, second, and third fields.
hypotheses: There is a particular representation witness x=m_x beta^q_x, with integers m_x and q_x satisfying -beta^p < m_x < beta^p and emin <= q_x <= emax, such that |y| <= (beta^p-beta/2) beta^q_x. Here beta and the integer mantissa are viewed as real numbers, beta/2 is real division, beta^p is a natural power, and beta^q_x is an integer power.

tr is an admissible run: s is a globally nearest representable value to the exact sum x+y; t is representable and no representable value lies in either half-open interval strictly from t toward the exact residual s-x; e is representable and no representable value lies in either half-open interval strictly from e toward the exact residual y-t; and each of x+y, s-x, and y-t has magnitude strictly below beta^p beta^emax.
mathematical_definitions: Let b be the real number obtained by casting the natural radix beta.
Let M=b^p, where p is the natural precision, and let scale(q)=b^q for every integer q.
A real z is representable exactly when there are integers m and q such that -M < m < M, emin <= q <= emax, and z=m scale(q), with m cast to a real.
Nearest(a,r) means r is representable and |a-r| <= |a-c| for every representable real c.
Adjacent(a,r) means r is representable and, for every representable c, neither r < c <= a nor a <= c < r holds.
An admissible run for tr=(s,t,e) requires Nearest(x+y,s), Adjacent(s-x,t), Adjacent(y-t,e), NoOverflow(x+y), NoOverflow(s-x), and NoOverflow(y-t).
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every permitted finite radix format, all real representable inputs x and y, and every admissible three-stage trace (s,t,e), suppose there is a representation x=m_x beta^q_x whose exponent makes |y| no larger than (beta^p-beta/2) beta^q_x. Then the second rounded quantity is exactly the residual s-x, the third rounded quantity is exactly y-t, the compensated sum s+e is exactly x+y, and the first-stage sum error satisfies |s-(x+y)| <= |y|.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The proposition is a chain of implications. It is vacuously true for any fmt, x, y, and tr for which representability, the witness-dependent size condition, or the admissible-run relation has no witness.
The separate assumption that x is representable is logically redundant with the existential size hypothesis, because that hypothesis already contains a representation witness for x.

The bound on |y| depends on the exponent of one existentially chosen representation of x. If x has multiple representations, it is enough that one exponent makes the inequality true; zero in particular can be represented with mantissa zero at every allowed exponent.
Representations are not required to be normalized or unique. Any integer mantissa strictly between -beta^p and beta^p is allowed, including zero, with any exponent in the inclusive exponent range.

The adjacent-rounding relation used for t and e is weaker than global nearest rounding: it excludes representable points between the chosen rounded value and the exact value but can choose the neighboring value on either side, even if the opposite-side neighbor is closer.
The nearest-rounding relation used for s permits ties because it requires only non-strict minimality and encodes no tie-breaking rule.
The run hypothesis assumes strict no-overflow bounds for the exact values x+y, s-x, and y-t; the proposition does not prove that such a run exists.
The expression beta/2 is division in the real numbers, not natural-number division or integer truncation.
The mantissa bounds and no-overflow bounds are strict, while exponent bounds and the main |y| and final-error bounds are non-strict.

Only scalar real arithmetic is modeled. No vectors, matrices, dimensions, other norms, relative-error measure, underflow behavior, subnormal classification, signed zero, infinities, NaNs, hardware evaluation order, or explicit IEEE rounding mode is encoded.
The conclusion does not say that s=x+y; it only bounds the first-stage rounding error. Exactness is asserted specifically for t and e, from which s+e=x+y follows.
